_comment_plant: Which implementation of IFSDSPlant stands behind the car. 'chaos' = Chaos observes the car it is already integrating (the only validated reference). 'shadow' = Chaos still DRIVES and the FMU is stepped alongside it with identical inputs, with divergence logged once a second; behaviour is unchanged by construction because nothing downstream reads the shadow. 'fmu' = the FMU is the plant, but the pawn is still Chaos-integrated, so the sensors describe a different car from the one on screen — bring-up only until the Phase 6 kinematic swap. See docs/fmu_plant_migration.md.

VehiclePhysics._comment_motor: MotorMaxTorque, MotorMaxPower, MotorRPM[], MotorTorque[] are vestigial. Drive torque comes from the dedicated UEmraxMotor class (EMRAX 228 MV at 400 V bus, see Plugins/FSDSPlugin/Source/FSDSPlugin/Public/EmraxMotor.h). The pawn silences Chaos's ICE-style engine each tick (SetThrottleInput(0)) and injects per-wheel torque via SetDriveTorque, so these fields feed only the silenced Chaos engine and have no effect on actual driving. Of the motor-side settings, only MaxRegenTorque/MaxRegenPower are forwarded to the EMRAX class. Kept here so existing tooling and external mirrors keep parsing; remove in a future pass.
VehiclePhysics._comment_regen: Regen is the ONLY braking channel on this car — there is no hydraulic service brake, and EBS is a separate pneumatic system on the handbrake channel. These two therefore define the entire service-deceleration authority of the vehicle. They were previously C++ defaults in FSDSSettings.h with no entry here, which meant the braking model was inheriting numbers nobody had chosen. MaxRegenTorque is the motor-side negative-torque cap; MaxRegenPower is the battery cell input-current limit and is the binding constraint at most speeds.

Sensors._comment_imu: BMI088-class noise model (the unit on the real IFS-08). Datasheet noise densities: accel 175 µg/√Hz, gyro 0.014 °/s/√Hz. At 400 Hz sample rate (200 Hz Nyquist BW) those become ~0.024 m/s² and ~0.0035 rad/s per-sample standard deviations. Bias drift is modelled as Ornstein–Uhlenbeck with a 100 s correlation time, a typical bench-test characteristic for a MEMS IMU at FS race-car operating temperatures.

Lidar1._comment_lidar: Hesai ATX_S01 datasheet (Section 1.4): 1-D rotating mirror (hybrid solid-state), 116 ch, 120° H × 18.3° V FoV (-12.4° to +5.9°), 10 Hz, ~1.74 M pts/s @ 0.08° H, 3 cm 1σ range. PointsPerSecond is the datasheet rate; the LiDAR stream is UDP-only since #322 (TCP and UDS senders retired — pre-#321 they existed to bypass macOS Docker Desktop's ~7 MB/s TCP loopback cap). The chunked, sender-paced UDP path holds ~7-8 Hz at the full datasheet rate; the remaining gap to nominal 10 Hz is in the DDS layer (1.4 MB BEST_EFFORT messages fragment-loss between publisher and subscriber) — tracked as a follow-up. Sensor packs only emit *hits*, so the wire rate is roughly 65 % of attempted rays (e.g. 1.14 M pts/s of valid range returns at 1.74 M attempted).
Lidar1._comment_maxrange: MaxRange in metres. Real Hesai ATX_S01 spec is 200 m. Set to 30 m for the sim because cones past 30 m don't matter for FS detection (max-corridor-width is well under that), and shrinking the per-ray broadphase distance is the cheapest UE5 CPU optimisation we have — Chaos walks the spatial hash for every actor along the ray's path, so a 7× shorter ray cuts the per-ray work by roughly that factor. Bump back to 200 for benchmarks against real-car captures or non-FS scenarios.
Lidar1._comment_mount: Mount aligned with the IFS-08's actual LiDAR position: X=0 (CoG-aligned, just beneath the main hoop), Y=0 (centered), Z=1.10 m (main hoop crossbar height). Previously X=0.5 m / Z=0.9 m was a hood-mount approximation; correcting it shifts the sensor back ~50 cm and up ~20 cm, which changes both the cone-detection range envelope (cones at the rear become visible) and the time-to-first-detection for cones immediately ahead. Verify cone_detection still classifies cluster heights correctly after re-baselining.
Lidar1._comment_lidarpath: GPU path (#223). Production default. Three-stage pipeline: depth render at the LiDAR's spherical scan envelope (CaptureScene), async GPU→CPU readback ring, and the FSDSLidarDecode.usf compute pass that turns depth texels into LiDAR-frame xyz hits. Output is the same flat-float point cloud the CPU path emits — switch to 'cpu' only for parity testing or a Chaos LineTrace reference run.
Lidar1._comment_perchannelmaxrange: Per-channel max-range overrides in METRES, indexed by V channel (0 = lowest V angle = -12.4°, 115 = highest = +5.9°). Real Hesai ATX_S01 has per-beam laser-power variance (datasheet App. A.1.1) — outer channels reach less far than central beams: 60 m bottom rings, 198 m centre, 90 m top. The array below is derived from the datasheet (App. A.1.2 Sorted by Ring IDs) and linearly remapped [60-198 m] → [25-30 m] so it fits under the sim's MaxRange=30 m perf budget while preserving the relative shape. Regenerate with `python3 tools/gen_per_channel_range.py --pretty`. Length must equal NumberOfChannels (116); mismatch logs a warning and falls back to MaxRange. Both CPU and GPU LiDAR paths read from this.
